integrated-mini-api-o3.counter_scope: The Mini object linked into each MK_STATS executable was emitted by the recorded llvm-api O3 compile command without --stats. compiler/backend/src/llvm/Lowering.kt sets inlineRc = rcPlan != null && !stats, so those objects use inline RC and only out-of-line mk_retain/mk_release runtime calls reach MK_STATS hooks. These retain/release figures are runtime-call counts, not total logical reference-count operations; the reported delta must not be described as an all-RC-op reduction. Allocation/free counters remain runtime managed-object counters. Fully instrumented LLVM emission would need a fresh --stats compile, which was not measured here.

stats_delta_integrated_vs_baseline.interpretation: Allocation/free and heap counters are runtime managed-object counters. Retain/release values and ratios compare only out-of-line runtime calls because the linked Mini objects were emitted without --stats and inline RC remained enabled; they do not represent all logical RC operations.

caveats: The integrated candidate combines NULL guarding, ArrayList default capacity 4, and LLVM API string fast paths; this baseline cannot assign a gain to any one change.
The Mini variants use their matching source stdlib/runtime compiled from Kotlin/C source at O2; this avoids mixing old published .mlib or runtime archives.
MK_STATS counters count Mini managed objects and reference events. They do not count the handwritten C reference malloc/realloc calls. Instrumented binaries are used only for counters, not timing.
Stats cover one REPS=5 execution per Mini variant; timing covers 2 warmups and 11 uninstrumented samples per variant.

The MK_STATS runtime was linked to objects emitted by llvm-api O3 without --stats. LLVM Lowering therefore kept inlineRc enabled, so retain/release counts cover only out-of-line runtime calls, not all logical RC operations; a fully instrumented LLVM compile was not run.

profile.variant: combined integrated Mini API O3; temporary REPS=50 source copy

exclusive_top_of_stack_collapsed.source_section: Sort by top of stack, same collapsed (when >= 5)
exclusive_top_of_stack_collapsed.semantics: exclusive sampled top frame per profile sample; rows are mutually exclusive top-of-stack buckets

inclusive_call_graph_nodes.semantics: sampled stack nodes include descendants and recursive frames; not additive with each other or with top-of-stack rows Max-per-node counts are not collapsed per function; the same function may occur in multiple stack nodes, so these values are not directly comparable to the exclusive collapsed totals.
inclusive_call_graph_nodes.dominant_observed_chain: mkh_user_main -> mk_release -> recursive mk_release -> ref_array_dispose -> recursive releases/free

private_string_buffer_fusion_evidence.proposal: Investigate a private string-builder buffer path that decodes/appends escaped strings directly and avoids intermediate substring/string allocations. The profile shows parser string handling, substring/allocation, StringBuilder append, and allocator functions on the exclusive top-of-stack list. Validate with identical checksums and MK_STATS before changing shared runtime behavior.

analysis.target_statement: The combined candidate improves median time about 10.5% from baseline (0.4920s to 0.4402s) but is still 1.361x the fastest matched strict C reference, above the 1.2x target.
analysis.source_provenance_note: The input JSON and expected output are byte-identical in both commits; each Mini binary compiled with the stdlib source files from the corresponding baseline/integrated commit and linked to runtime objects compiled from that same commit at -O2.
